models.name: Spicy Chicken
models.what: π0.5 trained on the recordings as they were, all five cameras

notes.title: How it was trained
notes.text: 15 to 16 October, in three stretches: it was stopped at 7,000 steps to stay inside a time budget and again at 8,000 for a reboot, and resumed from the saved checkpoint each time. Loss fell from 0.125 to 0.009.

notes.title: What it did on the robot
notes.text: At 7,000 steps both valid rollouts on 16 October put the vial in the right place. At 12,000 steps it left home in only 2 of 11 rollouts on 19 October; at 9,000 in 0 of 3.

notes.title: Why it froze
notes.text: Found on 19 October with offline tests on the GPU: about half of all frames at the home pose are the idle start of a demonstration and half the idle end, from the identical pose, so the policy told them apart from the pictures alone. In every demonstration the operator leaned over the robot at the start, and the policy learned that as its cue to move. Swapping just the wrist or the left_bottom image of a frozen rollout frame for a demonstration start made it reach.

models.name: Mango Rice
models.what: π0.5 trained from the base on a cleaned copy with one wording per move
models.data: vial-sort-slots-100, idle start and end cut, operator removed from the start frames, one canonical sentence per move

notes.title: What is different from Spicy Chicken
notes.text: The same recipe from the same base weights, with three changes to the data: the idle start and end of each demonstration are cut (58,650 frames became 46,361), about 8% of the samples at the home pose have the images that showed the operator swapped for views of the arm with nobody near it, and the 100 wordings are replaced by 32 canonical sentences, one for each move. It trained 4.1 passes over the data against 3.3.

notes.title: Tested every 1,000 steps without the robot
notes.text: Each checkpoint went through the offline gate (see the Training page). It leaves home at all 12; from 2,000 steps on its reach follows the source slot named in the command; it never follows the destination slot.

notes.title: On the robot, 21 October
notes.text: Run as RTC first, which never lifted the vial with this checkpoint, then in sync mode. In sync mode it took the right vial every time the command was worded exactly as in training, and put it in the asked slot in two of six rollouts, both slot 3.

models.name: Pretzel One
models.what: A 361-step fine-tune of Spicy Chicken to test the operator-free starts
models.data: vial-sort-slots-100, first trim (42,089 frames), operator-free start frames

notes.title: What it was for
notes.text: A test of the finding that Spicy Chicken froze at home because it had learned the operator leaning in as its cue to move. The first frames of each start were swapped for views with nobody near the arm.

notes.title: What went wrong
notes.text: It left home at once and grasped the right vial, but let go too early. The trim cut every demonstration at the first slight loosening of the gripper over the hole, before the vial was pushed in, so it learned to loosen over the rack and stop. The trim was corrected for Pretzel Two. The checkpoint was deleted on 22 October.

models.name: Pretzel Two
models.what: A 500-step fine-tune of Spicy Chicken with the corrected trim
models.data: vial-sort-slots-100, trimmed at the real let-go (46,361 frames), operator-free start frames

notes.title: What changed from Pretzel One
notes.text: The trim now cuts at the widest opening of the gripper after the grasp, which is the real let-go, and the fine-tune starts again from Spicy Chicken rather than from Pretzel One.

notes.title: Offline, before the robot
notes.text: It left home on all four frozen test frames (72 to 90 degrees against 3 for Spicy Chicken), kept the error at the moment of letting go at 1.5 degrees, and picked the right rack on 100% of training starts.

notes.title: On the robot, 19 October
notes.text: Its scored rollouts are in the table above. A separate table-top test of six prompts showed slot numbers barely read: a middle vial beat the asked number twice, and the destination digit pulled the reach toward the wrong source once. Destinations landed at slot 3 whatever the digit. The checkpoint was deleted on 22 October.

models.name: Crispy Falafel
models.what: FLUX 3 Action, LoRA fine-tune, overhead and wrist cameras
models.base: black-forest-labs/flux-3-action-so101, with this dataset's own joint ranges
models.data: vial-sort-slots-100, overhead and wrist cameras only

notes.title: How it was trained
notes.text: Run 1 from 14 to 15 October (0 to 10,000 steps, 5 h 42 min), run 2 from 18 to 19 October (10,000 to 30,000, 11 h 13 min, a checkpoint every 2,000). The learning rate is constant, so every checkpoint is a finished model. Loss fell from 0.249 to 0.087 and was flat from about 8,000 steps; 30,000 steps is 2.05 passes over the data.

notes.title: Getting it to run
notes.text: Three problems stacked on 14 October: the base repositories were re-published and asked for a new licence click, an attention library compiled for CUDA 13 silently fell back to a kernel that tried to allocate 882 GiB, and runs started from an interactive session were killed when the session ended. The first needed the cached revisions pinned, the second the CUDA 13 runtime put on the library path, the third a user-level systemd service.

notes.title: On the robot
notes.text: Always in sync mode: FLUX has no real-time chunking. It replans every 32 actions with a freeze of about 1.3 s, and ran at 15.5 Hz against the 30 Hz target. At 30,000 steps it grasped the asked vial in 4 of 4 grasps and put it in the asked slot in 1 of 4.

notes.title: Why only two cameras
notes.text: FLUX takes a scene view and a wrist view. The overhead camera was chosen on 14 October because it is the only high-angle view, has no people in it, and stays readable in the dark runs. The other cameras were not trained for FLUX.

camera_choice.intro: Three FLUX runs, each with a different scene camera. The choice of camera is the main thing that changed between them; they also differ in data size, training length and normalisation, so this is a sequence, not a controlled comparison.

rows.camera: Low side camera across the table, plus wrist
rows.result: Did not work. Deleted on 22 October.
rows.why: Black Forest Labs trained on high-angle views and dropped side views and datasets with people in them; this was a low side view with a person walking behind the table. The shipped joint ranges did not fit the arm either, and 3,000 steps on 5 demonstrations was too little.

rows.camera: The same camera re-aimed high and angled down, plus wrist
rows.result: Ran at 15 Hz with freezes. No success count was kept.
rows.why: A single task cannot show whether the prompt is followed. The wrist camera dropped off USB during one session.

rows.result: Right vial in 4 of 4 grasps at 30,000 steps; the right slot in 1 of 4.
rows.why: Source slots are read; destination slots are not (see Training). A rack of six slots covers about two of the 8 by 8 cells FLUX divides its picture into.

models.what: FLUX 3 Action on a single task, the first 25 demonstrations
models.base: black-forest-labs/flux-3-action-so101, with this dataset's own joint ranges
models.data: vial-flux25, one task ("take the vial from position 3 of the rack to the bin")
models.cams_note: left (re-aimed high) and wrist, from the earlier camera layout

notes.title: What it was
notes.text: The first FLUX run that used the arm's own joint statistics. 10,000 steps (2,500 updates), loss 0.345 to 0.089, 6 h 25 min on a GPU shared with other users' jobs. Its first launch died at step 141 for a reason never found.

notes.title: On the robot, 7 October
notes.text: Ran at 15.3 Hz, not 30: the 7-billion-parameter model takes 95% of each loop and froze for 1.3 s every 32 actions. Its rollouts were on the earlier scene layout, which the scoring script cannot read, so they are not scored on this site.

stages.label: Missed the vial
stages.def: The gripper never closed on the vial in the asked source slot: it closed on another slot, on an empty hole, or not at all.

stages.label: Grasped, not lifted
stages.def: The gripper closed on the right vial but the arm never lifted it.

stages.label: Lifted, let go elsewhere or not at all
stages.def: The arm lifted the right vial, then let go at a different slot or never let go before the rollout ended.

stages.label: Let go at the asked slot
stages.def: The arm let go at the slot the command asked for (within half a slot). It does not prove the vial ended in the hole: the scorer reads the arm, not the vial.
